title: KCET 2009 Maths
subject: maths
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: If $ax + by = 1$, where $a, b, x$ and $y$ are integers, then which one of the following is not true?
questions.explanation: Since $ax+by=1$, any common factor of $a,b$ must divide 1, so $(a,b)=1$; similarly $(a,y)=1$ (a prime dividing both $a,y$ would divide the sum, forcing it to divide 1). But $b$ and $y$ can share a common factor while $ax$ absorbs the rest, so $(b,y)=1$ need not hold.

questions.q: The digit in the unit place of the number $2009! + 3^{7886}$ is
questions.explanation: $2009!$ has $5$ and $2$ as factors many times over, so it ends in $0$. The units digit of $3^n$ cycles as $3,9,7,1$; since $7886 \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, $3^{7886}$ ends in $9$. So the sum ends in $0+9=9$.

questions.q: If $\begin{vmatrix} x+1 & x+2 & x+a \\ x+2 & x+3 & x+b \\ x+3 & x+4 & x+c \end{vmatrix} = 0$, then $a, b, c$ are
questions.explanation: Applying $R_1 \to R_1 - R_2$ and $R_2 \to R_2 - R_3$ gives rows $(-1,-1,a-b)$ and $(-1,-1,b-c)$; for the determinant to vanish identically these rows must be proportional, which forces $a-b=b-c$, i.e. $a,b,c$ are in A.P.

questions.q: The value of $\begin{vmatrix} 1 & \log_x y & \log_x z \\ \log_y x & 1 & \log_y z \\ \log_z x & \log_z y & 1 \end{vmatrix} =$
questions.explanation: Writing every entry in terms of natural logs, row 2 becomes a scalar multiple of row 1 after simplification (columns become proportional), so the determinant is $0$.

questions.q: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ then $|\text{adj } A| =$
If A and B are square matrices of the same order such that $(A+B)(A-B) = A^2 - B^2$, then $(ABA^{-1})^2 =$
questions.explanation: $(A+B)(A-B)=A^2-B^2$ forces $AB=BA$. Then $(ABA^{-1})^2 = AB(A^{-1}A)BA^{-1} = AB^2A^{-1} = B^2AA^{-1} = B^2$ using $AB=BA$.

questions.q: If $\vec a \cdot \vec b = -|\vec a||\vec b|$, then the angle between $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec a \cdot \vec b = |\vec a||\vec b|\cos\theta = -|\vec a||\vec b|$ gives $\cos\theta = -1$, so $\theta = 180^\circ$.

questions.q: If $\vec a + 2\vec b + 3\vec c = \vec O$, then $\vec a \times \vec b + \vec b \times \vec c + \vec c \times \vec a =$
questions.explanation: From $\vec a = -2\vec b - 3\vec c$: $\vec a\times\vec b = 3(\vec b\times\vec c)$ and $\vec c\times\vec a = 2(\vec b\times\vec c)$, so the sum is $6(\vec b\times\vec c)$; note $3(\vec c\times\vec a)=3\cdot2(\vec b\times\vec c)=6(\vec b\times\vec c)$ too, so options (1) and (3) give the same value.

questions.q: If the volume of the parallelopiped with $\vec a$, $\vec b$ and $\vec c$ as coterminous edges is 40 cubic units, then the volume of the parallelopiped having $\vec b + \vec c$, $\vec c + \vec a$ and $\vec a + \vec b$ as coterminous edges in cubic units is
questions.explanation: The volume with edges $\vec b+\vec c, \vec c+\vec a, \vec a+\vec b$ is always $2[\vec a\,\vec b\,\vec c] = 2\times40=80$.

questions.q: In the group $G = \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ under addition modulo 6, $(2 \oplus_6 3^{-1} \oplus_6 4)^{-1} =$
questions.explanation: The additive inverse of $3$ mod $6$ is $3$ itself. So $2+3+4=9\equiv3\pmod6$, and the inverse of $3$ is again $3$.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not true?
options: Identity element in a group is unique.
Inverse of an element in a group is unique.
Fourth roots of unity form an additive abelian group.
Cancellation laws hold in a group.
questions.explanation: The fourth roots of unity $\{1,-1,i,-i\}$ form a group under multiplication, not addition (they aren't even closed under addition), so statement (3) is false.

questions.q: The number of subgroups of the group $(Z_5, \oplus_5)$ is
questions.explanation: $Z_5$ has prime order, so by Lagrange's theorem its only subgroups are the trivial subgroup $\{0\}$ and $Z_5$ itself — 2 in all.

questions.q: The negation of $p \wedge (q \rightarrow \sim r)$ is
questions.explanation: $\sim[p\wedge(q\to\sim r)] = \sim p \vee \sim(q\to\sim r) = \sim p \vee (q \wedge r)$. (The question booklet printed this implication ambiguously, so KEA awarded a grace mark to everyone.)

questions.q: If $n = 2020!$, then $\dfrac{1}{\log_2 n} + \dfrac{1}{\log_3 n} + \dfrac{1}{\log_4 n} + \ldots + \dfrac{1}{\log_{2020} n} =$
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1}{\log_k n} = \log_n k$, so the sum is $\log_n(2\cdot3\cdots2020) = \log_n(2020!) = \log_n n = 1$.

questions.q: If 'n' is a positive integer, then $n^3 + 2n$ is divisible by
questions.explanation: $n^3+2n = (n^3-n) + 3n$; $n^3-n$ is a product of three consecutive integers and hence divisible by 3, and $3n$ is obviously divisible by 3, so the sum is always divisible by 3.

questions.q: On the set of integers Z, define $f: Z \to Z$ as $f(n) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{n}{2}, & n \text{ is even} \\ 0, & n \text{ is odd} \end{cases}$ then 'f' is
questions.explanation: $f(1)=f(3)=0$ (and $f(0)=0$ too), so it is not injective. But every integer $m$ is attained as $f(2m)=m$, so it is surjective. Hence $f$ is surjective but not injective.

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^2 + x + 1 = 0$, then $\alpha^{16} + \beta^{16} =$
questions.explanation: $\alpha,\beta$ are the complex cube roots of unity $\omega,\omega^2$. Since $\omega^3=1$, $\omega^{16}=\omega$ and $\omega^{32}=\omega^2$, so the sum is $\omega+\omega^2=-1$.

questions.q: The total number of terms in the expansion of $(x+y)^{100} + (x-y)^{100}$ after simplification is
questions.explanation: Odd-power terms cancel, leaving only even powers of $y$ from $y^0$ to $y^{100}$, giving $51$ terms.

questions.q: $\cot^{-1}(2\cdot1^2) + \cot^{-1}(2\cdot2^2) + \cot^{-1}(2\cdot3^2) + \ldots$ up to $\infty =$
questions.explanation: $\cot^{-1}(2n^2) = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{2n^2}\right) = \tan^{-1}(2n+1) - \tan^{-1}(2n-1)$, which telescopes to $\tan^{-1}(\infty) - \tan^{-1}(1) = \pi/2 - \pi/4 = \pi/4$.

questions.q: If 'x' takes negative permissible value, then $\sin^{-1} x$ is equal to
questions.explanation: For $x<0$, $\sin^{-1}x$ is negative while $\cos^{-1}\sqrt{1-x^2}$ is always non-negative, so $\sin^{-1}x = -\cos^{-1}\sqrt{1-x^2}$.

questions.q: If $1 + \sin x + \sin^2 x + \ldots$ up to $\infty = 4 + 2\sqrt3$, $0 < x < \pi$ and $x \neq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then $x =$
questions.explanation: The sum of the infinite G.P. is $\dfrac{1}{1-\sin x} = 4+2\sqrt3$, giving $\sin x = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, so $x = \pi/3$ or $2\pi/3$.

questions.q: The complex number $\dfrac{1+2i}{1-i}$ lies in
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1+2i}{1-i} = \dfrac{(1+2i)(1+i)}{2} = \dfrac{-1+3i}{2}$, which has negative real part and positive imaginary part, so it lies in the second quadrant.

questions.q: If P is the point in the Argand diagram corresponding to the complex number $\sqrt3 + i$ and if OPQ is an isosceles right angled triangle, right angled at 'O', then Q represents the complex number
questions.explanation: Since $OQ=OP$ and $\angle POQ = 90^\circ$, Q is P rotated by $\pm90^\circ$ about O, i.e. $P$ multiplied by $\pm i$: $i(\sqrt3+i)=-1+i\sqrt3$ or $-i(\sqrt3+i)=1-i\sqrt3$.

questions.q: The smallest positive integral value of 'n' such that $\left[\dfrac{1+\sin\frac{\pi}{8}+i\cos\frac{\pi}{8}}{1+\sin\frac{\pi}{8}-i\cos\frac{\pi}{8}}\right]^n$ is purely imaginary is, n =
questions.explanation: Writing $\sin(\pi/8)=\cos(3\pi/8)$ and $\cos(\pi/8)=\sin(3\pi/8)$, the bracket simplifies to $e^{i\cdot3\pi/8}$, so the expression is $e^{i\,3n\pi/8}$; this is purely imaginary when $3n\pi/8$ is an odd multiple of $\pi/2$, first satisfied at $n=4$.

questions.q: Which one of the following is possible?
questions.explanation: $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ must lie in $[-1,1]$ and $|\sec\theta|\ge1$, ruling out (1),(2),(3); but $\tan\theta$ can be any real number, so $\tan\theta=45$ is possible.

questions.q: If one side of a triangle is double the other and the angles opposite to these sides differ by $60^\circ$, then the triangle is
questions.explanation: With $a=2b$ and $A-B=60^\circ$, the sine-rule/tangent-rule relation for this data reduces to $C=90^\circ$, i.e. the triangle is right angled.

questions.q: $3(\sin x - \cos x)^4 + 6(\sin x + \cos x)^2 + 4(\sin^6 x + \cos^6 x) =$
questions.explanation: Using $(\sin x-\cos x)^2=1-\sin2x$, $(\sin x+\cos x)^2=1+\sin2x$ and $\sin^6x+\cos^6x=1-\tfrac34\sin^2 2x$, the expression simplifies (all $\sin2x$ terms cancel) to $3+6+4=13$.

questions.q: A cow is tied to a post by a rope. The cow moves along the circular path always keeping the rope tight. If it describes 44 metres, when it has traced out $72^\circ$ at the centre, the length of the rope is
questions.explanation: Arc length $= r\theta$ with $\theta = 72^\circ = \dfrac{2\pi}{5}$ radians, so $r = \dfrac{44}{2\pi/5} = \dfrac{220}{2\pi} \approx 35$ metres (using $\pi=22/7$).

questions.q: If $\begin{vmatrix} 1+\sin^2\theta & \cos^2\theta & 4\sin2\theta \\ \sin^2\theta & 1+\cos^2\theta & 4\sin2\theta \\ \sin^2\theta & \cos^2\theta & 4\sin2\theta-1 \end{vmatrix} = 0$ and $0 < \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then $\cos4\theta =$
questions.explanation: Subtracting row 1 from rows 2 and 3 and expanding gives the determinant $4\sin2\theta-2=0$, so $\sin2\theta=\dfrac12$; then $\cos4\theta=1-2\sin^22\theta=1-\dfrac12=\dfrac12$.

questions.q: The locus of the mid points of the chords of the circle $x^2+y^2=4$ which subtend a right angle at the origin is
questions.explanation: If a chord of $x^2+y^2=a^2$ subtends a right angle at the centre, the distance of the chord from the centre is $a/\sqrt2$, so the midpoint locus is $x^2+y^2 = a^2/2 = 2$.

questions.q: The length of the chord joining the points $(4\cos\theta, 4\sin\theta)$ and $(4\cos(\theta+60^\circ), 4\sin(\theta+60^\circ))$ of the circle $x^2+y^2=16$ is
questions.explanation: Chord length $= 2r\sin(\Delta\theta/2) = 2(4)\sin30^\circ = 4$.

questions.q: The number of common tangents to the circles $x^2+y^2-y=0$ and $x^2+y^2+y=0$ is
questions.explanation: Centres are $(0,\tfrac12)$ and $(0,-\tfrac12)$, both radius $\tfrac12$; the distance between centres is $1 = r_1+r_2$, so the circles touch externally and have 3 common tangents.

questions.q: The co-ordinates of the centre of the smallest circle passing through the origin and having $y = x + 1$ as a diameter are
questions.explanation: The smallest such circle has its diameter along the line with the origin at one end and the foot of the perpendicular from the origin to $x-y+1=0$ as centre; that foot is $(-1/2, 1/2)$.

questions.q: The length of the diameter of the circle which cuts three circles $x^2+y^2-x-y-14=0$; $x^2+y^2+3x-5y-10=0$; $x^2+y^2-2x+3y-27=0$ orthogonally, is
questions.explanation: Setting up the three orthogonality conditions $2gg_i+2ff_i=c+c_i$ and solving gives $g=-3,f=-4,c=21$, so the radius$^2=g^2+f^2-c=9+16-21=4$, radius $=2$, diameter $=4$.

questions.q: For the parabola $y^2=4x$, the point P whose focal distance is 17, is
questions.explanation: For $y^2=4x$, focal distance $= x+1 = 17 \Rightarrow x=16$, and $y^2=64 \Rightarrow y=\pm8$.

questions.q: The angle between the tangents drawn to the parabola $y^2=12x$ from the point $(-3, 2)$ is
questions.explanation: For $y^2=12x$ the directrix is $x=-3$; the point $(-3,2)$ lies on the directrix, and tangents drawn from any point on the directrix of a parabola are always perpendicular.

questions.q: The number of values of 'c' such that the line $y = 4x + c$ touches the curve $\dfrac{x^2}{4} + y^2 = 1$ is
questions.explanation: The tangency condition for $y=mx+c$ to $\dfrac{x^2}{4}+y^2=1$ is $c^2 = 4m^2+1 = 4(16)+1=65$, giving two values $c=\pm\sqrt{65}$.

questions.q: If the circle $x^2+y^2=a^2$ intersects the hyperbola $xy=c^2$ in four points $P(x_1,y_1)$, $Q(x_2,y_2)$, $R(x_3,y_3)$ and $S(x_4,y_4)$, then
questions.explanation: Substituting $y=c^2/x$ gives $x^4-a^2x^2+c^4=0$; since the $x^3$ coefficient is 0, the four roots sum to 0 (and their product is $c^4$, not $2c^4$, so options 3 and 4 are false).

questions.q: The foot of the perpendicular from the point $(2, 4)$ upon $x + y = 4$ is
The vertices of a triangle are $(6, 0)$, $(0, 6)$ and $(6, 6)$. The distance between its circumcentre and centroid is
questions.explanation: This is a right triangle (right angle at $(6,6)$), so the circumcentre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse $=(3,3)$; the centroid is $(4,4)$; the distance between them is $\sqrt{1+1}=\sqrt2$.

questions.q: The angle between the pair of lines $x^2 + 2xy - y^2 = 0$ is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Pair of Straight Lines
questions.explanation: Here $a=1,b=-1,h=1$, so $a+b=0$, which makes $\tan\theta$ undefined, i.e. $\theta=\pi/2$.

questions.q: $\lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \dfrac{3\cdot2^{n+1} - 4\cdot5^{n+1}}{5\cdot2^n + 7\cdot5^n} =$
questions.explanation: Dividing numerator and denominator by $5^n$: the terms with $(2/5)^n$ vanish as $n\to\infty$, leaving $\dfrac{-4\cdot5}{7} = \dfrac{-20}{7}$.

questions.q: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{\log(1+ax) - \log(1-bx)}{x}$ is not defined at $x=0$. The value which should be assigned to 'f' at $x=0$ so that it is continuous at $x=0$ is
questions.explanation: As $x\to0$, $\log(1+ax)\approx ax$ and $\log(1-bx)\approx -bx$, so $f(x) \to \dfrac{ax+bx}{x} = a+b$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = 1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}x^2 + \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6}x^3 + \ldots + x^n$, then $f''(1) =$
If $f(x) = \log_{x^2}(\log_e x)$, then $f'(x)$ at $x = e$ is
questions.explanation: Writing $f(x)=\dfrac{\ln(\ln x)}{2\ln x}$ and differentiating gives $f'(x)=\dfrac{1-\ln(\ln x)}{2x\ln^2x}$; at $x=e$, $\ln x=1,\ln(\ln x)=0$, so $f'(e)=\dfrac{1}{2e}$. (Grace marks were awarded to all, likely due to the ambiguous printed base notation.)

questions.q: If $y = \sin^n x \cos nx$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = n\sin^{n-1}x\cos x\cos nx - n\sin^n x\sin nx = n\sin^{n-1}x[\cos x\cos nx - \sin x \sin nx] = n\sin^{n-1}x\cos(n+1)x$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \dfrac{g(x)+g(-x)}{2} + \dfrac{2}{[h(x)+h(-x)]^{-1}}$ where g and h are differentiable functions, then $f'(0)$
questions.explanation: Both $g(x)+g(-x)$ and $h(x)+h(-x)$ are even functions of $x$, so $f(x)$ is even; the derivative of an even function is odd, and an odd function must vanish at $x=0$, so $f'(0)=0$.

questions.q: The tangent to a given curve $y = f(x)$ is perpendicular to the x-axis if
questions.explanation: A tangent perpendicular to the x-axis is a vertical line, i.e. its slope is infinite; equivalently $\dfrac{dx}{dy}=0$.

questions.q: The minimum value of $27^{\cos2x}\,81^{\sin2x}$ is
questions.explanation: The expression equals $3^{3\cos2x+4\sin2x}$; since $3\cos2x+4\sin2x$ ranges over $[-5,5]$, the minimum value is $3^{-5}=1/243$.

questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upwards from the top of a tower 64 metres high according to the law $s = 48t - 16t^2$. The greatest height attained by the stone above the ground is
questions.explanation: $s$ is maximum when $ds/dt=48-32t=0 \Rightarrow t=1.5$, giving $s_{max}=48(1.5)-16(1.5)^2=36$; total height above ground $=64+36=100$ metres.

questions.q: The length of the subtangent at 't' on the curve $x = a(t + \sin t)$, $y = a(1 - \cos t)$ is
questions.explanation: Subtangent $= y\dfrac{dx}{dy} = a(1-\cos t)\cdot\dfrac{1+\cos t}{\sin t} = a\dfrac{\sin^2 t}{\sin t} = a\sin t$.

questions.q: $\int e^{\tan^{-1}x}\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{1+x^2}\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Note $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[xe^{\tan^{-1}x}\right] = e^{\tan^{-1}x}\left(1+\dfrac{x}{1+x^2}\right)$, so the integral is $xe^{\tan^{-1}x}+c$.

questions.q: $\int \text{cosec}(x-a)\,\text{cosec}\,x\,dx =$
questions.explanation: Using $\sin a = \sin(x-(x-a)) = \sin x\cos(x-a)-\cos x\sin(x-a)$, the integral works out to $\dfrac{1}{\sin a}\log\left|\dfrac{\sin(x-a)}{\sin x}\right|+c$; options (2) and (4) are algebraically the same expression, so both are correct.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{x} |t|\,dt$, then for any $x \geq 0$, $f(x) =$
$\displaystyle\int_{1}^{3} \dfrac{\sqrt{4-x}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{4-x}}\,dx =$
questions.explanation: Using $\int_a^b f(x)dx = \int_a^b f(a+b-x)dx$ with $a+b=4$, the integrand transforms into its complement, so twice the integral equals $\int_1^3 1\,dx = 2$, giving the integral $=1$.

questions.q: The area bounded between the parabola $y^2=4x$ and the line $y=2x-4$ is equal to
questions.explanation: The curves meet at $y=-2,4$. Integrating w.r.t. $y$: $\int_{-2}^{4}\left[\dfrac{y+4}{2}-\dfrac{y^2}{4}\right]dy = 9$ sq. units.

questions.q: The differential equation of the family of circles passing through the origin and having their centres on the x-axis is
questions.explanation: Such circles are $x^2+y^2-2ax=0$; differentiating gives $a=x+y y'$, and substituting back into $a=(x^2+y^2)/2x$ gives $y^2=x^2+2xy\,dy/dx$.

questions.q: A population grows at the rate of 10% of the population per year. How long does it take for the population to double?
questions.explanation: $dP/dt=0.1P \Rightarrow P=P_0e^{0.1t}$; doubling needs $e^{0.1t}=2 \Rightarrow t = 10\ln2$.

questions.q: On the set of all natural numbers N, which one of the following $*$ is a binary operation?
questions.explanation: Only $a*b=a+3b$ is guaranteed to stay a natural number for all $a,b\in N$; the others can give negative, non-integer, or non-natural results.

questions.q: If $\displaystyle\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx = 5$, then the value of $\displaystyle\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx + 2^2\int_0^1 xf(x^2)\,dx + 3^2\int_0^1 x^2f(x^3)\,dx + \ldots + 10^2\displaystyle\int_0^1 x^9f(x^{10})\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: By the substitution $u=x^k$, $k^2\int_0^1 x^{k-1}f(x^k)dx = k\int_0^1 f(u)du = 5k$; summing $5k$ for $k=1$ to $10$ gives $5\times55=275$. (KEA awarded grace marks to all, likely because the coefficients were printed unclearly.)
